title: Second Word Happiness And Blessing In Belief Opening Comparison

questions.question: What does the passage say a person will find in believing in Allah?
questions.answer: Great happiness, blessings, pleasure, and ease.

questions.question: Why did the two men begin their trip?
questions.answer: For enjoyment and for business.

questions.question: What kind of path did the first man choose?
questions.answer: A selfish and bad path.

questions.question: What kind of path did the second man choose?
questions.answer: A godly and good path.

questions.question: What personal traits made the first man see things badly?
questions.answer: He was proud, self-centered, and negative.

questions.question: How did the first man view the land he entered?
questions.answer: He saw it as an evil and painful place.

questions.question: What kinds of people did the first man think he saw everywhere?
questions.answer: Weak and suffering people under cruel oppressors.

questions.question: What did the whole country seem like to the first man?
questions.answer: A place full of sorrow, like a house of mourning.

questions.question: What was the only escape the first man found from his sadness?
questions.answer: He thought drunkenness was the only way not to notice it.

questions.question: How did the first man feel about the people around him?
questions.answer: He saw them as strangers and enemies.

questions.question: What did he think he saw all around him besides enemies?
questions.answer: Dead bodies and crying, hopeless children.

questions.question: What was happening inside the first man because of his view?
questions.answer: His conscience was suffering deeply.

questions.question: What qualities did the second man have?
questions.answer: He was godly, devoted, fair-minded, and well-mannered.

questions.question: How did the second man see the same country?
questions.answer: He saw it as a beautiful and joyful place.

questions.question: What did he notice everywhere in that land?
questions.answer: Happiness, celebration, and gatherings of remembering Allah.

questions.question: How did the second man view other people?
questions.answer: He saw them as friends and like family.

questions.question: What two kinds of public events did he notice in the country?
questions.answer: Celebrations of people being released from duty and happy calls for new soldiers to join.

questions.question: How did the second man feel about his own joy and the joy of others?
questions.answer: He was glad about both.

questions.question: What practical benefit did the second man gain during the trip?
questions.answer: He made profitable business.

questions.question: What did he do after receiving these blessings?
questions.answer: He thanked Allah.

questions.question: What did the second man tell the first man was the real problem?
questions.answer: The ugliness inside him was making him see the outside world wrongly.

questions.question: According to the second man, what change did the first man need?
questions.answer: He needed to wake up, clean his heart, and see the truth.

questions.question: Why did the second man say the country could not truly be as terrible as the first man thought?
questions.answer: Because it belonged to a king who was just, caring, generous, powerful, orderly, and kind, and the country showed many signs of success.

questions.question: What happened to the unhappy man in the end?
questions.answer: He came to his senses, repented, and admitted he had been acting crazily because of drink.

questions.question: How did the unhappy man respond to the one who advised him?
questions.answer: He thanked him and said he had been rescued from a hell-like condition.

questions.question: What is the main lesson the story is used to explain?
questions.answer: That belief in Allah brings joy, goodness, and ease.

questions.question: How many travelers are in the comparison story?
questions.answer: Two.

questions.question: In what two ways were the men different at the start?
questions.answer: One was selfish and the other was godly.

questions.question: What made the first man’s journey turn dark in his own eyes?
questions.answer: His negative outlook made everything seem bad.

questions.question: What kind of rulers did the first man think controlled the land?
questions.answer: Cruel and oppressive rulers.

questions.question: What effect did his way of thinking have on the whole country in his eyes?
questions.answer: It made the whole place seem filled with grief.

questions.question: What does this show about how a person’s inner state affects what he sees?
questions.answer: A bad inner state can make the world look worse than it is.

questions.question: What was the first man unable to see in a healthy way?
questions.answer: The true meaning of what was happening around him.

questions.question: How did the second man’s character help him see differently?
questions.answer: His faith and good character helped him see beauty, friendship, and joy.

questions.question: What religious atmosphere did the second man notice in the land?
questions.answer: He saw places filled with remembering Allah and happiness.

questions.question: What sounds of happiness did he hear?
questions.answer: Good wishes, thanks, and words praising Allah.

questions.question: How did the second man understand the call to join soldiers?
questions.answer: He saw it as something happy and honorable.

questions.question: What is one difference between the two men’s views of other people?
questions.answer: One saw enemies and strangers, while the other saw friends and relatives.

questions.question: How did their different views affect their feelings?
questions.answer: The first lived in torment, while the second felt joy and peace.

questions.question: Besides spiritual happiness, what worldly success did the second man have?
questions.answer: He succeeded in trade.

questions.question: What did the second man do when he met the first man again?
questions.answer: He understood his condition and gave him sincere advice.

questions.question: What did he mean when he said the ugliness was inside the first man?
questions.answer: The first man’s bad inner condition was causing his false view.

questions.question: What did the adviser tell him to purify?
questions.answer: His heart.

questions.question: What would happen if that inner veil were removed?
questions.answer: He would be able to see reality correctly.

questions.question: What proof from the country did the adviser mention against the first man’s dark view?
questions.answer: The land showed clear signs of order, progress, and success.

questions.question: What change took place in the unhappy man after the advice?
questions.answer: He recovered his senses and turned back in repentance.

questions.question: What did the unhappy man admit about himself?
questions.answer: He admitted he had been acting crazily because of drink.

questions.question: What contrast between the two men best sums up the whole story?
questions.answer: One heart made the world look like a place of grief, and the other made it look like a place of joy.

questions.question: Which verse is mentioned near the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The verse about those who believe in the Unseen.

questions.question: What does the passage invite the reader to understand through a comparison?
questions.answer: How belief in Allah brings happiness, blessing, pleasure, and ease.

questions.question: What were the two men doing when the story began?
questions.answer: They were traveling.

questions.question: What was wrong with the first man’s way of looking at things?
questions.answer: He was selfish, arrogant, and gloomy.

questions.question: Because of that, what did the country seem like to him?
questions.answer: It seemed wicked and full of suffering.

questions.question: What kinds of scenes made him upset wherever he went?
questions.answer: He thought he saw helpless people crying under harsh oppressors.

questions.question: What image shows how sad the whole land looked to him?
questions.answer: It looked like one huge place of mourning.

questions.question: What unhealthy way did he use to avoid facing that sadness?
questions.answer: He turned to drink.

questions.question: How did he wrongly judge the people around him?
questions.answer: He treated them as enemies and outsiders.

questions.question: What does the passage say happened to his conscience?
questions.answer: It was in pain and torment.

questions.question: What four good qualities are given for the second man?
questions.answer: He was godly, devout, fair-minded, and of good character.

questions.question: How did the land appear to this second man?
questions.answer: It appeared excellent and full of goodness.

questions.question: What did he see happening everywhere instead of sorrow?
questions.answer: He saw celebration and joyful remembrance of Allah.

questions.question: How were people connected to him in his eyes?
questions.answer: They seemed like friends and relatives.

questions.question: What did he understand the celebrations to be about?
questions.answer: He saw them as happy events connected to finishing duties.

questions.question: What words of faith and praise did he hear?
questions.answer: He heard words glorifying Allah and declaring Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Did the second man only care about his own happiness?
questions.answer: No, he was happy for himself and for all the people there.

questions.question: What success in daily life did he also achieve?
questions.answer: He made beneficial business.

questions.question: After that success, what was his response?
questions.answer: He gave thanks to Allah.

questions.question: When the second man met the first again, what did he understand right away?
questions.answer: He understood the first man’s troubled condition.

questions.question: What basic message did he give the first man about his false view?
questions.answer: His inner corruption had colored what he saw outside.

questions.question: What two mistakes did he say the first man had made about what he saw?
questions.answer: He took joy as sorrow and took an orderly release from duty as violent destruction.

questions.question: What was the first man told to do so he could see correctly?
questions.answer: He was told to come to his senses and cleanse his heart.

questions.question: How did the first man respond after hearing this advice?
questions.answer: He repented and admitted his error.

questions.question: What kind of belief is highlighted in the passage by the quoted verse?
questions.answer: Belief in the Unseen.

questions.question: What does the passage connect with belief in Allah besides happiness?
questions.answer: Blessing, pleasure, and ease.

questions.question: What were the two men hoping to gain from their trip?
questions.answer: Enjoyment and business benefit.

questions.question: What inward problem shaped the first man’s whole experience?
questions.answer: His selfishness and dark outlook.

questions.question: Why is it important that the first man was pessimistic?
questions.answer: Because his pessimism made him misread everything around him.

questions.question: What did he think was happening to weak people in that land?
questions.answer: He thought they were suffering under cruel oppressors.

questions.question: What did he think had happened to many others?
questions.answer: He thought they had been destroyed.

questions.question: What does his seeing the whole country as a mourning place tell us?
questions.answer: He could not see any goodness or hope.

questions.question: What does the passage show about his relationship with society?
questions.answer: He felt cut off and saw everyone as hostile or strange.

questions.question: What emotional pain did this cause him inside?
questions.answer: It left his conscience in torment.

questions.question: What inner qualities gave the second man a better view?
questions.answer: Faith, devotion, fairness, and good manners.

questions.question: What did he see in the same land that the first man missed?
questions.answer: Rejoicing, worshipful remembrance, and happiness.

questions.question: How did he understand the people around him?
questions.answer: As friends and close companions.

questions.question: What sounds filled the country for him?
questions.answer: Sounds of celebration, gratitude, and praise to Allah.

questions.question: How did he react to the condition of the people and the events around him?
questions.answer: He felt pleased rather than crushed.

questions.question: What does his profitable trade add to the message of the story?
questions.answer: It shows that faith brings benefit in practical life too.

questions.question: Why did he thank Allah?
questions.answer: Because he recognized the blessings he had received.

questions.question: What did he tell the unhappy man about the source of his false vision?
questions.answer: It came from the darkness within his own self.

questions.question: What did the adviser say had to be removed from the first man’s eyes?
questions.answer: A veil of calamity caused by his inner condition.

questions.question: What kind of ruler did the adviser describe to prove the country could not be evil by nature?
questions.answer: A ruler who was just, merciful, generous, powerful, orderly, and kind.

questions.question: What evidence in the country supported that claim?
questions.answer: Many clear signs of development and success.

questions.question: What turned the first man away from his previous state?
questions.answer: Regaining his senses and repenting.

questions.question: What did he realize about the role of drink in his condition?
questions.answer: He realized it had driven him into madness.

questions.question: What did he say to the man who guided him?
questions.answer: He prayed good for him and thanked him for rescuing him.

questions.question: What does the passage promise to explain by using a story?
questions.answer: The joy and ease found in belief in Allah.

questions.question: What two different directions did the travelers take?
questions.answer: One took a selfish path, and the other took a godly path.

questions.question: Which traveler had a bad view of life, and why?
questions.answer: The first traveler did, because he was arrogant, self-centered, and gloomy.

questions.question: What kind of country did the first traveler think he had entered?
questions.answer: A harmful and miserable country.

questions.question: What suffering did he think he saw among the people?
questions.answer: He thought helpless and unfortunate people were crying under harsh tyrants.

questions.question: What did repeated scenes like that make the whole country seem to be?
questions.answer: One giant place of grief.

questions.question: How did the first traveler try to avoid seeing that painful picture?
questions.answer: He looked to drinking as an escape.

questions.question: In his eyes, what were the people around him like?
questions.answer: They were enemies and strangers.

questions.question: What sad images filled his surroundings?
questions.answer: Dead bodies and crying children with no hope.

questions.question: What happened to his conscience because of all this?
questions.answer: It was deeply troubled.

questions.question: What made the second traveler different in character?
questions.answer: He was faithful, devoted, fair, and good-mannered.

questions.question: What kind of country did the second traveler believe he was in?
questions.answer: A very good and beautiful land.

questions.question: What joyful things did he notice everywhere?
questions.answer: Festivals, remembering Allah, and happiness.

questions.question: How did he see the people of the land?
questions.answer: As friends and relatives.

questions.question: What did he hear connected with both finishing duty and beginning service?
questions.answer: He heard cheerful sounds of celebration, thanks, and calls praising Allah.

questions.question: How did his feelings differ from the first traveler’s feelings?
questions.answer: He felt joy and contentment instead of sorrow and pain.

questions.question: What successful work did he manage to do during the journey?
questions.answer: He completed profitable trade.

questions.question: What was his response after his good experience?
questions.answer: He thanked Allah.

questions.question: When he met the first traveler again, what did he understand?
questions.answer: He understood that the man’s problem was in his own inner condition.

questions.question: What did he say had happened between the first man’s inside and outside view?
questions.answer: The ugliness inside him had been reflected onto the world he was looking at.

questions.question: What examples did he give of the first man’s mistaken understanding?
questions.answer: He had taken laughter for crying and an orderly release from duty for looting and destruction.

questions.question: What did he urge the first man to do first?
questions.answer: Wake up and cleanse his heart.

questions.question: What would happen if he did that?
questions.answer: The false covering over his sight would be lifted and he would see the truth.

questions.question: How does the description of the king support the second traveler’s argument?
questions.answer: A land ruled by such a just and kind king would not truly be chaotic and evil.

questions.question: What was the final condition of the first traveler after the advice?
questions.answer: He repented, admitted his error, and felt rescued from a hell-like state.

questions.question: What phrase from the Qur’an appears in the passage before the story begins?
questions.answer: The phrase about believing in what cannot be seen.

questions.question: What four good things are linked to belief in Allah in this passage?
questions.answer: Happiness, blessing, pleasure, and ease.

questions.question: Why is the story called a comparison?
questions.answer: Because it shows two different kinds of people and how they see the same kind of journey very differently.

questions.question: What was the first traveler’s attitude centered on?
questions.answer: Himself.

questions.question: How did that selfish attitude affect what he expected and noticed?
questions.answer: It made him expect evil and notice only pain and darkness.

questions.question: What kind of cries and suffering did he imagine around him?
questions.answer: He imagined helpless people lamenting under oppression.

questions.question: What did he think was happening across all the places he visited?
questions.answer: He thought the same painful disaster was everywhere.

questions.question: What larger mood covered the whole country in his eyes?
questions.answer: Deep mourning and sadness.

questions.question: What did this show about his ability to trust or feel close to others?
questions.answer: He could not trust them and felt separated from everyone.

questions.question: What signs of hopelessness did he think he saw around him?
questions.answer: He thought he saw corpses and children crying without hope.

questions.question: What was the spiritual effect of this on him?
questions.answer: His inner self was in torment.

questions.question: What qualities of heart did the second traveler have?
questions.answer: He had faith, devotion, fairness, and good manners.

questions.question: How did these qualities change what he saw in the land?
questions.answer: They helped him see goodness, joy, and closeness instead of fear and grief.

questions.question: What role did remembrance of Allah play in his view of the country?
questions.answer: He saw the land as full of gatherings and joy connected to remembering Allah.

questions.question: How did he understand the people around him in social terms?
questions.answer: As companions, friends, and relations.

questions.question: What did the sounds of praise and declaration of faith mean to him?
questions.answer: They showed cheerful worship and meaningful purpose.

questions.question: How was his emotional state different from the first man’s state?
questions.answer: He was happy and content, while the first man was miserable.

questions.question: What extra success shows that his way was beneficial in more than one way?
questions.answer: He also did well in trade.

questions.question: What faithful response followed his success?
questions.answer: He thanked Allah.

questions.question: What truth did he point out when speaking to the unhappy man?
questions.answer: That the man’s own inner ugliness had distorted his sight.

questions.question: What does the advice about purifying the heart teach?
questions.answer: A clean heart helps a person understand reality correctly.

questions.question: What argument did he make from the character of the king?
questions.answer: A kingdom ruled by a just, caring, and orderly king would not truly be the nightmare the first man imagined.

questions.question: What argument did he make from the condition of the country itself?
questions.answer: Its clear signs of progress and accomplishment proved there was order and goodness there.

questions.question: What two changes happened in the first man at the end?
questions.answer: He regained his senses and repented.
